title: Quick check: Scrolling and Measuring Elements

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Scrolling and Measuring Elements”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Scrolling to sections should be used as a narrow imperative bridge while keeping normal UI declarative.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Scrolling to sections should be used as a narrow imperative bridge while keeping normal UI declarative.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Scrolling and Measuring Elements: Scrolling to sections should be used as a narrow imperative bridge while keeping normal UI declarative.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Scrolling to sections?
options: Check ref.current before use and avoid using refs to store display data that should trigger a render.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Check ref.current before use and avoid using refs to store display data that should trigger a render.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Scrolling and Measuring Elements: Check ref.current before use and avoid using refs to store display data that should trigger a render.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Scrolling and Measuring Elements” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Scrolling and Measuring Elements: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
